messages:
sasha: Heads up — deploy-bot flagged a large p95 spike in EU dedicated pool during the v2.3.1 canary. Thinking staged hold + manual extract (rollback) for that pool. Tagging ops for quick decision. :eyes:
deploy-bot: ALERT: canary_telemetry EU-dedicated — p95=720ms (+85%), error_rate=4.2% (threshold=1.0%). Autopilot suggestion: traffic_unwind -> revert to last stable. Reason: latency_p95_threshold.
sasha: Do we want autopilot to do it or manual? last false positive came from internal traffic fanout last week.
carla: I'd prefer manual here. Pause traffic to EU dedicated, pin pool to v2.3.0, and prepare customer comms. Who will own release-notes rollback bullet? :hand:
ben: I can run the pin. Prefer manual so we control cache warmup and KV invalidation timing. I'll stand by.
mike: Agree manual. We should avoid a hard rollback if it's a transient infra spike. Quick checklist: traces, KV cache heatmap, kernel flags.
david: Clarify — are we reverting model weights or just routing back to v2.3.0?
ben: Just routing/traffic pin. No DB/schema changes. KV compat check passed last run.
sasha: @deploy-bot, can you apply a staged hold (reduce to 30%) while we confirm?
deploy-bot: ACK command from sasha. action=staged_hold start. target_split=30% over=2m. reason="p95 spike - verify".
carla: Drafting customer note now: short, apology, what we did (traffic pin), mitigation ETA=2h, contact. Will post in #customer-success for review.
ben: Executing manual pin: `redwoodctl traffic pin --pool eu-dedicated --version v2.3.0 --reason "p95 spike during canary"`
deploy-bot: ACTION COMPLETE: traffic_pin applied by ben. pool=eu-dedicated version=v2.3.0 new_split=100% timestamp=5222223410
eva: Re-running smoke + regression tests against pinned version now, ETA ~12m.
sasha: Great. @carla please notify affected customers (list in RT-4567). Add a rollback bullet to release notes: "rolled back regional canary to v2.3.0 due to p95 latency spike; investigating".
carla: Sending comms now, cc'ing sales & support. Also creating incident ticket for postmortem.
mike: I'll own the postmortem. Initial suspects: kernel change + aggregation skew in the new routing. Will capture traces and KV heatmaps.
david: If we see evidence it's infra (host-level), we may want to re-run canary on a fresh host pool instead of immediate code change.
sasha: Agreed. For now we keep manual control. If we confirm safe, we'll rollforward with a small canary on a fresh host group.
carla: Comms sent to customers + internal thread in #customer-success. Adding a short FAQ: what happened, what we changed, ETA, next updates.
ben: Leaving notes in the release ticket with commands used and exact timestamps.
sasha: Thanks all. We'll keep this thread as the single source of truth for timeline and comms. Escalate to SOC if any security anomalies show up in traces. :thumbsup:
